name: Sangam India Ltd
title: Sangam India Ltd - 514234 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Sangam India FY26 revenue crossed INR3,200 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR83 crore; Q4 PAT INR33 crore on INR880 crore revenue.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a rebuild year, with revenue, EBITDA and PAT rising sequentially from Q1 through Q4. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR880 crore, EBITDA INR98 crore and PAT INR33 crore. Management attributed profit growth to high capacity utilisation and operational efficiency, and denied any one-time inventory gain in Q4 despite the West Asia war lifting crude-linked input prices. Management is preparing a new capex cycle but has not finalised it; renewable power and captive fibre are the stated priorities.

financial_highlights.change: rose QoQ each quarter of FY26 per management
down from 80 days in one year

segments.name: Yarn (cotton and polyester)
segments.commentary: Yarn is about 50% of revenue, split roughly evenly between cotton and PV (polyester-viscose) yarn, so cotton is about 25% of total revenue. Yarn capacity utilisation is about 95%. PV yarn is mostly domestic, with 10-15% exports; March shipments to some regions were delayed and freight costs rose.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Garment utilisation is about 50%, the highest in six to eight quarters, with management expecting further gains. C9 brand accounts for 40-45% of garment business and contract manufacturing for the balance.

segments.name: Recycled polyester fibre
segments.commentary: In-house recycled fibre meets about 50% of polyester fibre needs, processing close to 40,000 metric tons of plastic waste a year. Green fibre is reported at about 97% utilisation. Management targets 75-80% in-house share.

segments.name: Denim fabric
segments.commentary: About 50% of denim raw material is sourced in-house; management plans more capacity here.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to double PAT again in FY27 but called it an aspiration, not a commitment.
FY27 top-line growth expected to be similar to FY26, with no abnormal growth given high utilisation; management said the March quarter revenue times four plus price inflation is the base.
Renewable power share expected to rise from about 10-15% now to 70%+ by around June 2027, with cumulative EBITDA benefit of INR50-60 crore annually once commissioned.
June quarter margins expected to be maintained or better than March quarter; management declined to give a number.
Management said new capex benefits will not come in FY27; energy-cost savings are the only FY27 benefit from current projects.
Order book stated at 50-70 days across segments; about two-thirds or more of exports are on FOB terms.
capex_capacity: Committed renewable capex about INR150-160 crore plus about INR30-35 crore of PPA equity infusion, totalling about INR200 crore.
New capex is at planning stage with a two-year planning cycle; no concrete plans or financing (preferential issue) decided.
Capacity additions planned across segments except garments (garment utilisation about 49-50%); focus on existing plants, no greenfield.
Yarn utilisation about 95%; green fibre about 97%.
Management said it would take about a quarter to plan the next capex and that a new capex cycle would come after a large capex cycle three years ago.
demand_pricing: Demand improving over the past six months, stronger than a year ago, per management.
War-driven price increases began around 10-15 March; management said Q4 saw little price impact, and that most cost increases have been passed on so far.
Exports go to 50+ countries; regional focus varies by product (Bangladesh and China for some, Africa/Egypt/Turkey for others, Latin America for others).
Management said yarn exports are being reduced by strategy and shifting to fabric exports.
No premium is earned on recycled-fibre (ESG) yarn in the domestic market; some European buyers may pay one.
Polyester fibre from Reliance is about 5% of supply, so the quality control order removal had little effect on raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 PAT driven by one-time inventory gains from war-driven price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; orders are booked 60-75 days ahead and pre-war orders from Jan-Feb were serviced, and little price movement hit Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook after the doubling-PAT aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-line growth similar to FY26 (run-rate of Q4 times four plus inflation); no abnormal growth expected given high utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renewable energy share and EBITDA benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable share about 10-15% now, targeted at 70%+ by around June 2027; cumulative EBITDA benefit INR50-60 crore annually once commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: What share of garment revenue comes from C9 brand?
qa_highlights.answer: C9 brand contributes 40-45% of garment business; contract manufacturing the balance.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any PLI incentive in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Benefits are not factored in; complications exist. Management said any PLI benefit would be a one-time gain, and the incentive is about INR100 crore turnover scale, not INR200-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and export billing terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is 50-70 days across segments; two-thirds or more of exports are FOB, with new bookings factoring current freight costs.

risks_watch: Crude and West Asia war effects on input costs (dyes, chemicals, packaging, freight); management said it plans only a week to a fortnight ahead.
Possible one-time gains or losses from crude-linked inventory and old orders with freight losses.
Capex plan and funding for FY28 onward not yet defined; preferential issue ruled out for now.
Debtor days still elevated versus two years ago; management said debtor reduction is a focus area.
Customer count decline flagged by an analyst; management did not address it on the call.
Garment utilisation (about 50%) remains the lowest segment utilisation; PLI benefit not included in plans.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and FY26 execution, but cautious and evasive on FY27 specifics: capex, margins, war-driven price effects and PLI were answered with 'not concrete yet' or 'dynamic scenario'. Management repeatedly framed FY27 PAT doubling as an aspiration.
key_quotes: We're now meeting approximately 50% of our polyester fiber requirement through in-house recycled production, processing close to 40,000 metric tons of plastic waste annually.
I would not agree that the current quarter PAT is driven by any kind of one-time inventory gains.
Probably in a year's time, let's say June next year is when we expect that about 70% plus of our power will be renewable.
So, it will be a two-year cycle for the new capex that we want to plan.

adds.what: Renewable power capacity to lift renewable share of power to 70%+ (committed capex ~INR150-160 crore plus ~INR30-35 crore PPA equity)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 top-line growth similar to FY26 with no abnormal growth, and an aspiration (not commitment) to double PAT again; backing is high utilisation (~95% yarn), order book of 50-70 days, and renewable power savings of INR50-60 crore annually from June 2027, while new capex is deferred with no FY27 volume benefit.
